biography.plain_text: Basil Manuel Mavroleon was a Greek shipowner who built London & Overseas Freighters with his Kulukundis cousins. Based in London, he helped turn their shipping interests toward modern tankers and led the company onto the stock exchange. His career linked an established family shipping network with the financing of a larger fleet.

long_biography.plain_text:
Basil Manuel Mavroleon, the driving force behind London & Overseas Freighters, began in his cousins’ shipping agency as an office boy and messenger. Chartering became his speciality, and he spent much of his working life at the Baltic Exchange arranging employment for ships. During the Second World War, he stayed in Britain with John Kulukundis to manage their vessels under the Ministry of War Transport.

His experience as an owner also shaped shipbuilding. At Austin & Pickersgill, he championed a practical replacement for ageing wartime Liberty ships: the standard SD14 cargo vessel. The design offered owners a relatively economical new ship, and Mavroleon encouraged Greek customers to place orders. More than two hundred were eventually built in Britain and overseas. He remained chairman of London & Overseas Freighters until his death, having relinquished the managing director’s position after a heart attack.
